evidence: The backlogRun doc comment asserted that a run reopens after an interruption, and the three original tests only covered contiguous runs, so a seen-once refactor would have passed them. 3308b99 adds TestBacklogReopensARunAfterAnInterruption (A, B, A order, asserting A's epic and claim lines each appear twice), and the agent reports mutating openingRun to the seen-once form to show the test then fails.
guidance_note: When a doc comment names a behavior that separates two plausible implementations (adjacency vs seen-once), write the test that tells them apart in the original PR.

evidence: The original entry ends with 'still prints every context line it did before.' and has no ticket ref, while neighboring entries end with one. 3308b99 appends '(links-listing-x943)'.
guidance_note: Before adding a CHANGELOG bullet, copy the shape of the adjacent bullets, including the trailing ticket reference.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here. 3308b99 only added a test and the changelog ref, and the preamble line 'a row with no epic line belongs to the epic named above it' is already in the round-0 diff hunk. The premise holds: sortByCompositeRank interleaves standalone leaves with epic children, so a leaf with no epic can sit right under an epic's run. Instead of the reviewer's softer wording, the agent emitted 'epic: none' at run boundaries, which brings back the meaning the suppression removed and makes the preamble rule literally true.
guidance_note: When suppressing a repeated line, list every situation in which the blank now appears before writing the rule that tells the reader what a blank means.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here. The line `claim: openingRun(claim, here.lane.String(), above.lane.String())` is unchanged context in the 1aa2bcb diff, so it predates review. The premise holds: LaneID.String joins epic and key with '#', so distinct lanes can render alike. bd20fb7 widens openingRun's subject to comparable and compares LaneID directly, which is the reviewer's fix plus removing the constraint that forced the stringification. It adds a test that fails on revert.
guidance_note: Never use a display rendering (a String() documented 'for logs and test failures') as an identity key; compare the comparable value itself.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here. The phrases 'rank order that is already on screen' and 'nothing is hidden' are in the original entry, and 1aa2bcb only appended the epic: none sentences. The premise holds because the agent confirmed pendingSiblingsByEpic is deliberately unfiltered, so under --assignee or --limit the named sibling can be off-screen. bd20fb7 drops the overclaim and also fixes the same claim in the nearestPendingLaneMate comment and the preamble.
guidance_note: Before writing a 'nothing is hidden' or 'already on screen' claim about a view, check it against every filter and limit flag that view accepts.

evidence: F3's fix (1aa2bcb) rewrote the preamble to 'An epic line and a claim line ... a row without one continues the run above it' but added the disambiguating marker only for the epic line, which left the claim line's blank ambiguous between 'same claimed lane' and 'different unclaimed lane'. The agent concedes 'I fixed this exact defect for the epic line one round ago and did not carry it across.' It measured that a symmetric marker would add noise, since every standalone row is its own lane, and instead fires 'unclaimed' only when a claim is standing above.
guidance_note: When fixing an ambiguity for one of several values that share a mechanism (openingRun serves both epic and claim), check every sibling value against the same failure before pushing.

narrative: This PR prints group-scoped backlog facts once per run. Rounds 1-3 raised issues that were present in the original commit (a missing reopen test, a false preamble universal, String()-keyed lane identity, a changelog overclaim under filters), even though three of them carry ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flags because the code only sat beside the fix commits. Round 4 is the one fix-caused round: F3's epic: none fix restated the preamble rule for both the epic and claim lines but disambiguated only the epic line, and the reviewer then found the identical gap on the claim line. Every response checked the premise, and several picked better cures than the reviewer proposed.
guidance_observations: The agent's habit of mutation-testing each new test (reverting the fix to confirm the test fails) appears on F1, F4 and F6 and is worth keeping.

Each of the four rounds after the first found a distinct gap in the original design of run suppression, which suggests an up-front pass over what a suppressed blank can mean would have collapsed several rounds into one.
On F5 the agent swept the same overclaim from two other sites it had written, which is the move it did not make on F3 and which F6 then cost a round.

evidence: The plugin.json diff adds author/homepage/repository/license/keywords, while marketplace.json gains only owner.url and a new description, so 'both manifests carry real ... metadata' is false. There was no thread reply, but the issue comment says it was reworded in d889710, and the claim was still present when round 1 re-raised it as F3.
guidance_note: When a CHANGELOG line says 'both' or 'each' about a set of files, check the claim against each file's diff before committing.

evidence: The ON-POST-REVIEW-COMMIT flag is a false positive here. The round-0 summary already describes this skip-when-absent test, and c64c05c's CHANGELOG context carries #491's merged text, which marks it as a rebase rather than a fix. The test comment's 'same posture ... toward the optional dolt binary' is misleading if CI installs dolt but not claude, which the agent confirmed. The agent corrected the comment in d889710 and filed links-templates-qq4i.1 to wire claude into CI rather than doing that here.
guidance_note: When justifying a test skip by analogy to an existing optional dependency, check whether CI actually provisions both before writing the analogy.

evidence: This repeats F1 on the same unchanged sentence. It is not fix-caused: no fix for F1 had landed, and c64c05c (a rebase) left the 'both manifests carry' wording intact. It was fixed with F1 in d889710.
guidance_note: Address open findings before pushing a rebase that triggers a new review, so the round is not spent re-raising them.

narrative: This PR presents the repo as a Claude Code plugin marketplace. Round 0's changelog overclaim (F1) got no reply, and a rebase push (c64c05c) triggered round 1, which re-raised it (F3) and added a fair point that the skip-based validation test never runs in CI (F2). Both were answered in one issue comment and fixed in d889710, with CI wiring deferred to a filed ticket. None of the findings came from a fix.
guidance_observations: Pushing a rebase while a round-0 finding was still open bought a review round whose only new content was F2.
Responses went into a single PR issue comment rather than the threads, which leaves each thread's resolution unanchored to a commit.

evidence: The hunk shows inline() wrapping lines in quotedInlineOpen/Close, while quoteRemote only ran envelopeDefuser (the agent-instructions tags) over the text, so a remote id containing '»' closed the token early. 28783fe extends the defuser to every emitted delimiter, keyed on the constants. It also rejects the naive '<<' mapping because '«agent-instructions>' would assemble a live tag, and it adds tests for both cases.
guidance_note: When introducing a new delimiter around untrusted text, add it to the escaping set in the same change; a boundary is only a boundary if the payload cannot contain it.

evidence: stripControls used unicode.IsControl (Cc only), while its own comment frames the threat as hiding or repainting the ESCALATION line on a terminal, which bidi overrides (Cf) also do. 28783fe rejects category Cf too and names the ZWJ/ZWNJ collateral.
guidance_note: When a sanitizer's comment states a threat model, derive the reject set from that threat (anything that reorders or hides text), not from the nearest stdlib predicate.

evidence: The hunk shows 'Base-absence alone CANNOT decide it' rewritten to 'Base presence cannot stand in for it either', followed by an argument about the combine path feeding an empty base, which is about absence. The agent confirms it flipped the word in 240367c and restored 'absence'.
guidance_note: After shortening a paragraph's topic sentence, reread it against the sentences that follow to confirm it still states their claim.

evidence: This duplicates F1 (a literal '«'/'»' in a remote value escapes inline()'s bounding) and also asks for the 'newline' break token to be covered. 28783fe's delimiterDefuser covers all five delimiters, keyed on the constants. The one-source-of-truth citation fits: keying the defuser on the same constants the emitter uses stops a renamed delimiter from drifting out of the escaper.
guidance_note: When introducing a new delimiter around untrusted text, add it to the escaping set in the same change, keyed on the same constant the emitter uses.

narrative: This PR closes #490's review findings: it classifies id collisions by created_at and hardens the untrusted-text quoting. Round 0 found that the new inline guillemets were not themselves defused (raised twice, F1 and F4), that the control-strip missed Cf characters, and a comment word flipped by this PR's own rewrite. All four were fixed in one commit (28783fe) with tests the agent showed failing at HEAD~1, and round 1 approved with no findings.
guidance_observations: The agent rejected the obvious '<<'/'>>' escaping after spotting that it could assemble a live delimiter, which shows it checking the cure separately from the diagnosis.
Tests asserting the property over the delimiter constants (TestDefusedTextCarriesNoDelimiter) turn a future missed delimiter into a test failure instead of a review finding.
